name: Glycerin
indication_description: Glycerin suppository is used for the relief of occasional constipation.
pharmacology_description: Glycerin is a hyperosmotic laxative, given rectally, which usually produces a bowel movement within 15 minutes to 1 hour. Hyperosmotic laxatives encourage bowel movements by drawing water into the bowel from surrounding tissues. This produces a softer stool mass and increases bowel action. These products are used for fast, predictable relief of occasional constipation.
dosage_description:
Children under 2 years: As directed by the physician.
Children (2 to 6 years): Only 1 Glycerin 1.15 Suppository per day or as directed by the physician.
Adults and Children (From 6 years): Only 1 Glycerin 2.30 Suppository per day or as directed by the physician

Insert suppository well up into the rectum. Suppository does not need to melt completely to produce laxative action.
contraindications_description: Sensitivity to the ingredients. Do not use unless the patient to be treated is, in fact, constipated.
side_effects_description: When glycerin used rectally may cause rectal discomfort or a burning sensation.
pregnancy_and_lactation_description: Pregnancy category C. There are no controlled data in human pregnancy.
storage_conditions_description: Keep below 25°C temperature, away from light & moisture. Keep out of the reach of children.
